source.title: Data Separability for Neural Network Classifiers and the Development of a Separability Index
source.authors: Shuyue Guan; M. Loew; Hanseok Ko

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains neural networks on synthetic datasets and measures training difficulty/accuracy, but its experiments do not use random labels or unstructured inputs. Its results bear on the broad claim about fitting data and training difficulty, using different datasets and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2016) for slower convergence on random labels; that cited result is not this study's own evidence. Its own results concern synthetic cluster datasets and image preprocessing, not randomly labeled training sets.
record.test_reason: The only random-label convergence finding is attributed to Zhang et al. (2016). This study measures training distinctness and separability on labeled synthetic clusters and preprocessed CIFAR images; it supplies no results testing V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the conclusion that DSI indicates distributional similarity and is an effective separability measure in the tested datasets. The authors also acknowledge that their separability concept does not represent general training difficulty: Figure 10 gives approximately equal DSI (0.3472) but different TD values (0.96 and 0.79).
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train networks on synthetic cluster datasets and preprocessed CIFAR images to evaluate training distinctness and data separability; they do not apply random-label or unstructured-input training interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training distinctness varies with cluster standard deviation; for CIFAR datasets, preprocessing condition changes TD and complexity measures. The paper reports that (1 − DSI) tracks the ordering of preprocessing conditions, while several other measures are nearly flat or behave differently.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger synthetic-cluster standard deviations yield lower normalized average training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested FCNN, increasing cluster overlap reduces training distinctness.

fits_no_version.finding: For preprocessed CIFAR datasets, 1 − DSI increases across conditions ordered by decreasing training distinctness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed separability measure tracks training distinctness across the tested image preprocessing conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-output DSI exceeds input DSI, while some hidden-layer DSIs fall below input DSI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DSI need not increase monotonically across the tested FCNN's layers.

record.problems: The results relevant to training behavior are largely plotted without numeric values in the text. The paper does not test any of the six claim versions; random-label convergence appears only as a citation to Zhang et al. (2016). The CIFAR text gives inconsistent architectural summaries between Section 4.2 and Appendix 7.2.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Results cited from Zhang et al. (2016) are excluded because they are not this paper's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, near-zero final training error, chance test performance and unchanged architecture/hyperparameters.
Random-versus-true label training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of explicit regularization on random-label fitting and generalization after removing regularization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own correctly identified lack of tests of V1–V6. Neither the Random dataset's complexity scores nor randomly partitioned airplane-image DSI measurements establish neural-network memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on completely random labels or report test error at chance.
Does not compare training time for random labels versus true labels, or vary corrupted-label fractions.
Does not train on shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not vary random label corruption or report training and test error across corruption rates.
Does not test random-label fitting with or without weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, nor generalization on true labels after their removal.
Does not compare learning of real patterns with memorization of noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: fully-connected neural network (FCNN) model
rows.size_stated: three hidden layers, with 16, 32, and 16 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Trained on each of nine two-class synthetic datasets for 1,000 epochs; training accuracy averaged as TD and normalized as rTD.
rows.measure: rTD, the normalized average training accuracy during training
rows.value: Figure 4 only; text states rTD is lower for datasets with larger cluster SDs.
rows.note: No individual rTD values are stated in text; the reported qualitative trend is that larger cluster SD corresponds to lower rTD.
rows.check: The qualitative rTD trend is reported, but varying cluster overlap does not constitute random-label corruption. Average training accuracy also does not establish final training error or time to convergence.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers, two max-pooling layers, and one dense layer (Appendix architecture describes two FC layers)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 images after five image preprocessing methods; TD measured for each processed dataset.

conditions.value: Color (factor=2) and Sharpness (2), Color (2), Contrast (2), Color (0.1), and Contrast (0.5)

rows.measure: TD and complexity measures, including (1 − DSI)
rows.baseline: Original images included as a condition; individual TD values not stated.
rows.value: Figure 6 only; text states (1 − DSI) monotonically increases from left to right as TD decreases.
rows.note: Results are shown in a figure without numeric values in the text. The text describes preprocessing effects on data separability and CNN performance, not random-label fitting.
rows.check: Preprocessing preserves class labels and does not produce the unstructured inputs named in V3. Appendix 7.2 specifies two fully connected layers, dropout, RMSprop and 200 epochs. Complexity measures use a 1,000-image subset; CNN training uses 50,000 images.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers, two max-pooling layers, and one dense layer (Appendix architecture describes two FC layers)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 images after five image preprocessing methods; TD measured for each processed dataset.

conditions.value: Color (factor=2) and Sharpness (2), Color (2), Contrast (2), Color (0.1), and Contrast (0.5)

rows.measure: TD and complexity measures, including (1 − DSI)

rows.check: This experiment uses CIFAR-100's 20 superclasses, not its 100 fine classes. Appendix 7.2 specifies two fully connected layers and 200 epochs. Complexity measures use a 1,000-image subset; CNN training uses 50,000 images. No random labels or unstructured inputs are tested.

rows.subject: three-layer FCNN model
rows.size_stated: three-layer; exact neuron counts not restated here
rows.operation_detail: Measured DSI of input and outputs from each layer after training on each of nine synthetic datasets.

conditions.value: nine two-class synthetic datasets from Section 4.1.2

rows.measure: DSI of input and layer outputs
rows.value: Figure 9 only; text states final output DSI is always higher than input DSI, while some hidden-layer output DSIs are smaller than input.
rows.note: A measurement of separability across network layers; no numeric values stated in text.
rows.check: DSI across layers measures representation separability after training, not real-versus-noisy label learning over training. The reused FCNN has three hidden layers of 16, 32 and 16 neurons.
